summary: The staged code matches the supplied implementation, but the browser verification does not establish all acceptance criteria and localhost port conflicts are unhandled. The supplied results show 37 passing tests; independent browser inspection was denied by browser security policy, and build/tests were not rerun in the read-only environment.

issues.problem: The script claims all acceptance criteria pass without checking several required behaviors. Mobile checks only inspect canvas width and a counter, so clipped or overlapping controls pass. It omits the 60-second auto-fire stress test and subsequent complete cleanup. Network monitoring starts after navigation and ignores Network.loadingFailed, allowing failed resource loads to escape detection. buildResult is hard-coded rather than established by a build result.

issues.required_change: Attach monitoring before navigation and capture failed requests. Verify control bounds and overlap at both required viewports, focused-button Enter/Space activation, sustained auto-fire with resource limits, and complete cleanup after disabling auto-fire. Run the production build and record actual build/browser results; report unverified checks explicitly.

issues.problem: The application port is fixed at 4173. Any existing HTTP 200 response is assumed to be this application's production server; an occupied port returning another status leads to an unhandled listen error. scripts/serve.js likewise has no port-conflict recovery. This violates the planned occupied-port handling and can verify the wrong application or prevent verification entirely.
